method: Read by hand in the release file (bootstrap.js: startup, launchBackendIfNeeded, provisionEnvironment, the uv lookup, downloadStandaloneUv, ensureVcRedistWindows) and the README, after the developer's response (issues/9); every quote checked against the release file and README; level from the fixed rule; label and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
label: Downloads uv, and on Windows Microsoft's C++ runtime installer, when it first sets up its Python
summary: The first time Zotero starts with it, it sets up its own Python: it downloads uv from Astral's GitHub releases if it can't find one on the computer, and on Windows, only when Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime is missing, that runtime's installer from Microsoft, which asks for administrator rights. Its README says both. Neither file is checked beyond its size and type.

facts.what: uv, the Python package manager from Astral (the latest release, from github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/), unless uv is already on the computer; uv then installs Python 3.13 (Astral's own Python builds) into the plugin's data folder. On Windows only, when vcruntime140_1.dll is missing, the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable (x64) installer from Microsoft's official link aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe (it redirects to download.visualstudio.microsoft.com), run with /install /passive /norestart through PowerShell's Start-Process -Verb RunAs, so Windows asks for administrator rights, then deleted.
facts.publisher: Astral, who make uv, and Microsoft, who make the Visual C++ runtime
facts.readmeQuote: Requires the [Microsoft Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable (x64)](https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe) for native document conversion and ONNX runtime dependencies (setup automatically detects and installs it if missing).
facts.readmeQuote2: the extension automatically provisions an isolated, hermetic Python `3.13` runtime and `.venv` via [Astral `uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)
facts.notes: startup() (line 11) calls launchBackendIfNeeded() (line 276). With no .venv yet (line 2751), provisionEnvironment() runs: ensureVcRedistWindows() (2114) returns at once off Windows or when isVcRedistInstalledWindows() finds vcruntime140_1.dll; otherwise it shows 'Installing Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime (24 MB)...' in the sidebar's setup card, fetches the aka.ms link (2135), rejects files of 5 MB or less or without an MZ header, and runs it elevated (2185). The uv lookup tries a system uv, the plugin's own bin folder and ~/.local/bin and ~/.cargo/bin before downloading the latest standalone uv (1873, 1658); the download is rejected under 1 MB and the binary's magic bytes are checked, nothing more. 'uv python install 3.13' (2229) then fetches Python through uv. The plugin's own Python package is a wheel shipped in the .xpi (backend/zocrates.whl) and its dependencies are held to backend/constraints.txt, 223 exact versions exported from uv.lock; that install is the separate package-run finding.
facts.reviewerNote: Both downloads come from the program's maker over https and the README names both, so CAP-DOWNLOAD-EXEC-MAKER (low), as for jadense-in-zotero and iris-zotero's uv downloads. uv is the latest release rather than a fixed version, and nothing checks either file against a fingerprint; that's within the rule, which treats the maker's own https download as installing it yourself.
